name: The Scientific Revolution and the People Who Made It
description: How a few curious Europeans, from Copernicus to Newton, replaced old authority with measurement and experiment and started modern science.

checkpoints.name: A new sky and a new body
checkpoints.note: Copernicus moves the Sun to the centre of the planets, and Vesalius opens up the human body to see what is really there. Tycho Brahe then begins to measure the heavens with unmatched care.

checkpoints.name: Telescopes and experiments
checkpoints.note: Kepler turns Tycho's numbers into laws of planetary motion, Galileo sees moons around Jupiter, Bacon argues for experiment, Harvey explains the blood and Descartes tries to rebuild knowledge on reason.

checkpoints.name: Societies and microscopes
checkpoints.note: Boyle, Hooke and Huygens work with air pumps, microscopes and clocks. Leeuwenhoek sees tiny living things, and the Royal Society gives scientists a place to share and test findings.

checkpoints.name: Newton's world
checkpoints.note: Newton's Principia shows that one law of gravity governs apples and planets. Halley predicts a comet, Leibniz and Newton quarrel over calculus, and Émilie du Châtelet spreads Newton's ideas on the Continent.
